take: Hurricane Isaias has shut in 1.46m b/d of US Gulf crude production, 71% of offshore output, and with Brent already above $100 and Trump putting Iran strikes on hold ahead of the midterms, the supply-side buffer is thinner than the headline record 13.8m b/d US crude average suggests, so any duration extension on shut-ins tightens the prompt spread. The US has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel for six months via General License 135 through 7 April 2027 whilst Russia and Germany add barrels, and China plans to resume refined fuel exports, which together cap the distillate squeeze that has been the real tightness in the complex. Positioning-wise, the diesel crisis persists despite record crude output because refinery configuration cannot convert light sweet into middle distillate at will, and the FSL LR1 sale to UAE interests at $110m alongside Larine's exit signals asset owners are monetising tanker strength rather than betting on further product tightness. The cross-market link to watch is bunker: ammonia bunkering trials and CMB.TECH's 210,000 dwt Mineral Europa maiden voyage to Australia point to structural tonne-mile demand growth on the dry side, whilst Black Sea grain exports cratering amid maritime war cuts both tonne-miles and the diesel demand that goes with them. In the next 24 hours, watch Isaias landfall timing and the Marine Minerals Service restart guidance, the Panama Canal authority's post-earthquake inspection results for transit continuity, and whether the Trump-Putin diesel détente holds through the weekend.
